name: What should be included in an office build-out scope of work?

mainEntity.name: What items should be listed in the scope so an office build-out estimate is actually comparable?
mainEntity.text: What items should be listed in the scope so an office build-out estimate is actually comparable?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clear scope of work is essential because office build-out pricing can vary dramatically depending on what is actually included. At a minimum, the scope should describe demolition, framing, drywall, doors, glazing, ceiling systems, flooring, paint, lighting, power and data, HVAC modifications, plumbing, restrooms, millwork, fire protection, permitting, cleanup, and final inspections. It should also specify who is responsible for design coordination, landlord approvals, permit corrections, and testing of any life-safety or mechanical systems. In the Los Angeles area, many cost disputes happen because one proposal assumes reuse of existing items while another includes full replacement. When the scope is precise, owners can compare bids fairly and avoid low bids that leave out important work. This is especially important for build-outs in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, where building conditions and landlord requirements can vary widely.
